---
title: Edges
description: How one item links to another, what each edge type means, and what the bin does across a link.
---

An **edge** links one item to another: it points **from** one item **to** another, such as a comment to the lease it's about. It's a record of its own, with an `id`, properties and a [version](/build/versions), so writing an edge never moves either item's version.

```http title="Request"
POST /edges
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "from_id": "01a1f144-e102-7276-97a9-e93846d7cf4e",
  "to_id": "01a1f144-e0da-77a3-a1c4-ead9c1e9d53c",
  "edge_type": "comments-on"
}
```

A new item can carry its edges: `POST /items` takes `edges`, an object from each edge type to the IDs it points to. If Marfa refuses any edge, it creates neither the item nor its edges.

## Edge types

Every edge has an **edge type**, and the type sets the rules:

- **Which types each end can be.** An `in-collection` edge points to a container, and an `in-folder` edge to a folder.
- **How many edges an end holds**, its cardinality. `many-to-one` lets each from item hold at most one edge of the type, so a comment is on one item and a message in one thread. `one-to-many` lets each to item hold at most one, so a child has one parent. `one-to-one` limits both ends, and `many-to-many` neither.
- **Whether its edges can loop.** No edge links an item to itself, and `parent-of` and `supersedes` refuse any loop.
- **What the bin does across it**, as [Moving an item to the bin](#moving-an-item-to-the-bin) shows.
- **Its labels**, the headings an app shows at each end.

A write that breaks one is refused with `400 edge_constraint_violation`, or `400 edge_cycle` for a loop. Marfa ships eleven, which the Catalog's [Edges](/catalog/edges) page lists with each one's limits and how a [synced folder](/use/sync-a-folder) writes it. A key whose metadata map holds `edge_types=write` can [register more](/api-reference/edge-types/registerEdgeType).

### Choose an edge type

Start from what the link means to a person:

- **One item sits under another**, as a subtask under its task: `parent-of`. Its children go to the bin with it. To gather items without owning them, as recipes in a collection, use `in-collection`, and an item can be in many collections.
- **An item exists only for another**, as a comment, a reply or a receipt photo for an expense: `comments-on` or `attached-to`, which make it a [part](#parts). For an item that stands alone, as a note about a film, use `about`.
- **A message belongs to a thread**, as an email to its thread: `in-thread`, with `position` for its order. A conversation that holds its messages as [table rows](/build/tables) needs no edges.
- **One item's text links to another**, a **mention**: `references`. A device reads `[[Plan]]` in a note and writes a `references` edge to Plan.
- **An item was taken or made from another**: `excerpt-of` for a passage taken from it, as a highlight from a book, which carries its own text and stays when the book goes. Use `derived-from` for something made from it, as a summary from an article.
- **A new item replaces an old one**, as this year's lease replaces last year's: `supersedes`. Each item replaces at most one and is replaced by at most one.

Marfa writes `in-folder` itself, for the files a synced folder places.

## Parts

Some items exist only for another: a comment, a reply, a scan's pages, a receipt attached to an expense. Such an item is a **part**, and the item it belongs to is its **host**. `attached-to` and `comments-on` make parts, and a registered edge type can too.

**Would you look for it on its own?** If not, make it a part. If you would, as with a photo in an album, use another edge type.

A part follows its host into the bin: it goes once its last host goes, and comes back when any host is restored. Listings still include parts, so an app that wants them out filters with `part eq false`. Archiving a host, or deleting the edge, leaves the part where it is.

## Read an item's edges

An item read carries its outbound edges in `edges`, up to 50 of each type. Add `include=backrefs` for the edges that point to it, and `include=neighbors` for the items at the other ends. [List an item's edges](/api-reference/edges/listItemEdges) and [List an item's backrefs](/api-reference/edges/listItemBackrefs) page through the rest.

A key reads an edge only when it may read the edge type, which its [edge map](/build/access#what-a-credential-reaches) grants, and the item it points from.

## Moving an item to the bin

An edge type's `cascade_on_delete` decides what the bin does across its edges:

- **`cascade`, on `parent-of`.** Moving a parent to the bin takes its children with it, at every depth, and never the other way.
- **`with-hosts`, on `attached-to` and `comments-on`.** A part goes with its last host, as [Parts](#parts) explains.
- **`orphan`, on the other eight.** The other item stays active, and so does the edge.

So a note moved to the bin takes its child note and its comments, and leaves the book it's `about` where it is.

<BinCascade />

A registered edge type can also choose **`block`**: while such an edge holds an item, at either end, moving that item to the bin is refused with `400 edge_constraint_violation`, and `details.blocking_edges` names the edges. So is a delete that would take it there along a cascade. Delete the edge first. A purge is never blocked: it deletes the item's edges.

The rules behind this page are in the [edges](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/edges.md) chapter of the contract.
